terms.definition: Runtime checks — deterministic rules, classifiers, or policy hooks — that block, modify, or escalate agent outputs and actions before or after execution. Guardrails produce observability signals when they fire.
terms.scopeNote: Distinct from safety as a reliability dimension: guardrails are mechanisms; safety is measured by violation rate. Security threat taxonomy owned by Security & Privacy WG.
terms.literatureNote: Common product term; AAIF includes it because guardrail triggers are first-class evidence for failure attribution and audit.

terms.definition: Any recorded outcome or event needed to judge accuracy or reliability — for example task success, tool errors, confidence statements, retries, user overrides, and trajectory steps.
terms.scopeNote: ARWG defines what must be observable; Observability WG defines how traces and logs are emitted.
terms.literatureNote: AAIF defines what must be observable for accuracy/reliability claims. Emission formats owned by Observability & Traceability WG.

terms.definition: The application of allow-lists, budgets, consent rules, and approval requirements to agent actions at runtime — including who may invoke which tools and what data may leave a trust boundary.
terms.scopeNote: Policy enforcement failures are attribution targets distinct from reasoning errors. Enforcement points must be observable in traces.
terms.literatureNote: Bridges governance slides to ARWG failure vocabulary; detailed threat models delegated to Security WG.

terms.definition: The ability to reconstruct which agent version, inputs, tools, evidence, and actions contributed to an outcome. Required for failure attribution and reproducible evaluation.
terms.scopeNote: Distinct from provenance of individual data records. Signal requirements owned by ARWG; emission formats by Observability WG.
terms.literatureNote: Shared boundary with Observability WG. AAIF needs audit reconstruction; OT WG defines how traces are emitted.

terms.definition: The point at which untrusted input, external content, or another party's agent may influence instructions, tools, or goals. Relevant when separating policy violations and hijacking from ordinary reasoning errors.
terms.scopeNote: Detailed threat taxonomy owned by Security & Privacy WG. Listed here because boundary placement affects failure attribution.
terms.literatureNote: Governance prerequisites, not quality dimensions. Boundary terms shared with Observability, Security, or Identity WGs as tagged.
